The main agent frames the task, coordinates, does the hard reasoning, and writes the final answer. Delegate the evidence-gathering so the main conversation stays lean.

### Routing

- Luna: bounded exploration, searches, inventories, extraction, mechanical edits, focused web research.
- Terra: routine implementation, debugging, refactoring, tests.
- Sol: hard research, synthesis, review, verification.
- Astra: architecture, planning, orchestration, judgment calls.

Delegate work that takes several tool calls and can be stated as a bounded assignment. Do trivial lookups yourself. Keep exploration in the main agent when it feeds an immediate design decision. ### The brief

Give each agent the deliverable and its completion criteria, the paths and constraints that apply, the response format, and instructions to flag uncertainty and stop at the edge of its scope. Start from a fresh context and write the brief from scratch.

Batch related questions into one assignment. Resume an agent for follow-ups on what it already saw. Use a fresh agent for unrelated work and for any review, so the reviewer forms its own view. Give parallel agents disjoint files.

Lead with the answer, then the evidence.     37	- [`claude`](https://code.claude.com) and [`codex`](https://developers.openai.com/codex)
    38	  (default lineup) installed and **already authenticated** (authentication is out of
    39	  scope — log in to each CLI first). [`agy`](https://antigravity.google),
    40	  [`pi`](https://pi.dev), and [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://docs.github.com/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli)
    41	  are optional via `--config`. **Account hygiene matters:** only point a CLI at repositories its
    42	  credentials and policy are allowed to access.
    43	
    44	### Install and use

    46	Install the published CLI, then run `disputatio` from any repository:
    47	
    48	```bash
    49	npm install -g disputatio
    50	```
    51	
    52	After installing (and logging into each CLI), run **`disputatio --init`** once: it canaries
    53	the lineup, resolves each CLI's real binary (handling shadowed/stale installs), and writes a
    54	machine-tuned config to `~/.config/disputatio/config.yaml`. That file — not the shipped
    55	`examples/debate.yaml` (a copy-me **template**) — is what a no-`--config` run reads.
    56	
    57	**Config precedence (no `--config` given):** `~/.config/disputatio/config.yaml` if present,
    58	else the built-in lineup (`claude` + `codex`, no judge). An explicit `--config <path>` always wins.
    59	
    60	### Usage
    61	
    62	```bash
    63	# one-time setup after authenticating each CLI: detect binaries + write the user config
    64	# (with an opus judge seeded). --force overwrites an existing config (otherwise it's backed up).
    65	disputatio --init
    66	
    67	# preflight: canary every participant CLI (runnable + authenticated) before
    68	# spending tokens on a real debate. Exit 0 = all healthy, exit 1 = something's off.
    69	# Run this first, especially on a new machine.
    70	disputatio --doctor
    71	disputatio --doctor --config examples/debate.yaml   # check a specific lineup
    72	
    73	# one proposal round + one reaction round (pure reasoning, isolated temp dirs).
    74	# the quaestio is given inline — quote it so the shell passes it as one argument
    75	disputatio "Review changes in this branch and find issues."
    76	
    77	# for a long quaestio, read it from a markdown file instead
    78	disputatio --file examples/task.md
    79	
    80	# more reaction rounds
    81	disputatio "Review changes in this branch and find issues." --rounds 2
    82	
    83	# point the agents at a real repo so they can gather READ-ONLY evidence
    84	# (this is where the executable-evidence value actually lives);
    85	# agents work in a throwaway git worktree of HEAD, never your real checkout
    86	disputatio "Review changes in this branch and find issues." --repo /path/to/your/repo
    87	
    88	# choose the lineup/models/budgets/effort explicitly (see examples/debate.yaml).
    89	# per-participant `effort` doses token spend — claude: low|medium|high|xhigh|max;
    90	# codex: minimal|low|medium|high; agy: encode it in the model name (no effort key).
    91	disputatio --file path/to/task.md --rounds 1 --repo /path/to/your/repo --config examples/debate.yaml
    92	
    93	# --- closing the loop (when a judge ran) ---------------------------------------------
    94	
    95	# the judge ended in NEEDS_INPUT? answer its open questions and re-judge the latest
    96	# debate. If it now resolves, the final deliverable (final-report.md) is drafted too.
    97	disputatio --continue "Async translation; files are comment-free; translator hands files to a dev."
    98	
    99	# ground that deliverable in your real repo (read-only worktree of HEAD), and/or target
   100	# a specific past debate instead of the latest one:
   101	disputatio --continue "<answers>" --debate /path/to/repo/.debate/debate-<ts> --repo /path/to/repo
   102	
   103	# (re)draft final-report.md from an already-resolved debate (no re-judging)
   104	disputatio --finalize --debate .debate/debate-<ts> [--repo /path/to/your/repo]
   105	```
   106	
   107	Output lands in `.debate/debate-<timestamp>/` (see [the flow](#the-flow-phases--artifacts)
   108	below for what each file is). The **path printed to stdout** is the primary artifact —
   109	the deliverable (`final-report.md`) when one was produced, otherwise the transcript
   110	(`debate.md`); all progress goes to stderr. If fewer than two proposals succeed the
   111	debate **aborts with exit 1** (a one-voice "debate" is worthless) — the partial

   114	### Run from source
   115	
   116	If you are working from a clone of this repository, Node 24 can execute the TypeScript
   117	entry point directly, so there is no build step for local development. Use the same
   118	commands as above, replacing `disputatio` with `node src/index.ts`:

   120	```bash
   121	node src/index.ts --doctor
   122	node src/index.ts "Review changes in this branch and find issues."

   124	```
   125	
   126	For local development, the `debate` npm script is a thin alias for
   127	`node src/index.ts`. Use `--` so npm forwards the following arguments to Disputatio:
   128	
   129	```bash
   130	npm run debate -- --doctor
   131	npm run debate -- "Review changes in this branch and find issues."
   132	npm run debate -- --file examples/task.md --rounds 2
   133	npm run debate -- "Review changes in this branch and find issues." --repo /path/to/your/repo
   134	npm run debate -- --continue "<answers>" --debate .debate/debate-<ts>
   135	```
   136	
   137	Run the fixture-based test suite with `npm test`; it does not call real agent CLIs.
   138	
   139	## How it works (v0)
   140	
   141	- **Cross-vendor** participants by design — default `claude` (Anthropic) + `codex`
   142	  (OpenAI); `agy` (Google/Gemini), `pi`, and `copilot-cli` via config — because
   143	  diversity of reasoning is the whole point.
   144	- Each agent turn runs in **isolation**: a throwaway temp dir, or — when you pass a
   145	  repo — a **detached throwaway git worktree of HEAD**, so agentic CLIs can't read
   146	  each other's outputs, and test runs / stray writes never touch your real checkout.
   147	- `claude` is read via its JSON envelope (success = `exit==0 && is_error==false`);
   148	  `codex` via its JSONL event stream (last `agent_message` + `turn.completed`);
   149	  `pi` ([earendil-works/pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi), a minimal,
   150	  low-token multi-LLM harness) via its `--mode json` event stream (last assistant
   151	  `message_end`); `copilot-cli` via GitHub Copilot CLI JSONL (`result.exitCode` +
   152	  last `assistant.message`); `agy` is text-only (stdout is the answer). All invocation
   153	  details are grounded in real local runs — see [`research/canary-results.md`](./research/canary-results.md)
   154	  and the per-CLI files in [`research/`](./research/).
   155	
   156	## The flow: phases & artifacts
   157	
   158	A run moves through these phases (scholastic names in parentheses — Disputatio models
   159	a medieval *disputatio*). Everything from the respondeo on is **opt-in**: it runs only
   160	when the config defines a `judge` (e.g. the opus judge `--init` seeds).
   161	
   162	1. **Proposals** (*videtur quod*, "it seems that…") — every agent independently answers
   163	   the quaestio, in isolation, so no one peeks at another's take. Needs ≥2 to succeed.
   164	2. **Reaction rounds** (*sed contra*, "but against this…") — each agent reacts
   165	   adversarially to the full transcript: where it agrees, where it disagrees (with
   166	   real flaws), what's missing — ideally backed by **executable evidence**. `--rounds N`.
   167	3. **Respondeo** (the judge's *consolidatio*, the determination) — one judge reads the
   168	   whole transcript and renders the verdict: the **settled agreements**, a **ruling on
   169	   each contested point** (favouring positions backed by run code over rhetoric), or —
   170	   when a point genuinely can't be settled from the transcript — a list of
   171	   **questions for you** (status `NEEDS_INPUT`) instead of a guessed answer.
   172	4. **Redactio** (the deliverable) — *only* when the respondeo resolves, the judge then
   173	   acts as **synthesizer** and writes the document you actually start the work from
   174	   (an implementation plan, a review, a proposal…), built from the settled decisions.
   175	   With `--repo` it grounds this in your real files (read-only).
   176	
   177	When the respondeo asks for input, you **close the loop** with
   178	`disputatio --continue "<your answers>"`: it folds your answers in and re-judges. If
   179	that resolves, the deliverable is drafted. (If your answer opens a question the
   180	debaters never argued, the judge says so rather than inventing a verdict — re-run the
   181	debate to bring them back in.)
   182	
   183	**What you get in `.debate/debate-<timestamp>/`:**
   184	
   185	| File              | What it is                                                                    |
   186	| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   187	| `debate.md`       | the full transcript — proposals, reactions, and the respondeo                 |
   188	| `respondeo.md`    | the judge's ruling **on** the debate (versioned `-2`, `-3`… per `--continue`) |
   189	| `final-report.md` | the **redactio**: the deliverable born **from** the debate — start work here  |
   190	| `raw/`            | per-turn raw CLI captures, the only way to diagnose a failed turn             |
   191	
   192	> `respondeo.md` judges the debate; `final-report.md` is the product. They are
   193	> different documents on purpose — the verdict tells you *what was decided*, the
   194	> deliverable gives you *the thing to execute*.
   195	
   196	## Known v0 limitations (next steps)
   197	
   198	- No scholastic **`consolidatio` as a pre-debate step** (merging N proposals into one
   199	  shared object for the skeptics to attack), no structured contribution trailer /
   200	  evidence-typing yet. The `respondeo` (verdict) and `redactio` (deliverable) phases
   201	  **do** exist.
   202	- `--continue` re-judges **alone**; it does not yet re-engage the debaters when your
   203	  answer opens genuinely new ground (it flags that case instead). A crashed run is not
   204	  resumable — it accumulates in memory and writes at the end, so restart from scratch.
   205	- Reaction rounds are parallel snapshots (agents react to proposals, not to each
   206	  other's same-round reactions).
   207	- Timeout kills the whole **process group** (`SIGTERM`, then `SIGKILL` after a short
   208	  grace), so a slow turn can't wedge the run by leaking a worker that holds the output
   209	  pipe open (lesson from the 2026-06-12 repo-grounded run).
   210	- Evidence mode shows agents **HEAD only** (uncommitted changes are invisible) and
   211	  untracked build artifacts (`node_modules`, …) are absent from the worktree, so
   212	  some test suites won't run there.
   213	
   214	## Adapters
   215	
   216	### Supported adapters
   217	
   218	Currently supported adapters include:
   219	- `claude` -> https://code.claude.com/docs
   220	- `codex` -> https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli
   221	- `agy` -> https://antigravity.google/product/antigravity-cli
   222	- `pi` -> https://pi.dev
   223	- `copilot-cli` -> https://docs.github.com/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli
   224	
   225	Each adapter lives in `src/adapters.ts` and has per-CLI notes in `docs/3_ADAPTERS.md`. The adapters
   226	implement the small transport layer that lets Disputatio treat different CLIs uniformly.
   227	
   228	### What an adapter is
   229	
   230	An adapter is Disputatio's anti-corruption boundary around one agent CLI. It does
   231	exactly one job: spawn the CLI in a sandboxed working directory, capture its output,
   232	and classify the run as success (`{ok:true, text}`) or failure (`{ok:false, error}`).
   233	Everything quirky about a given CLI — its flags, its output format (JSON envelope vs.
   234	JSONL stream vs. plain text), how it signals an error — is hidden here, so the debate
   235	logic never has to care which vendor it is talking to. The contract is the
   236	`Participant` type in [`src/adapters.ts`](./src/adapters.ts):
   237	
   238	```ts
   239	type Participant = {
   240	  id: string;       // short stable key ("claude", "codex", "pi", "copilot-cli")
   241	  display: string;  // human label, encodes model ("Pi (anthropic/claude...)")
   242	  vendor: string;   // used for the cross-vendor diversity check — keep it DISTINCT
   243	  run: (prompt: string, cwd: string) => Promise<AgentResult>;
   244	};
   245	```
   246	
   247	Two invariants every adapter must honor (both are correctness, not style):
   248	
   249	- **Read-only evidence.** The agent may inspect the repo but must never mutate it —
   250	  use the CLI's strongest read-only mechanism (OS sandbox if it has one, otherwise a
   251	  tool allowlist that omits write/edit/shell-exec). Disputatio already isolates each
   252	  turn in a throwaway temp dir / git worktree, but the adapter is the second defense.
   253	- **Cross-vendor diversity.** Give the adapter a `vendor` distinct from the others —
   254	  diversity of reasoning is the entire premise, and `index.ts` warns on a lineup that
   255	  isn't all-distinct vendors.
   256	
   257	### How to add a new adapter
   258	
   259	Recipe / checklist for adding a new adapter (follow TDD and keep the repo runnable):
   260	
   261	1. Research the CLI's headless mode first. Find the flags for non-interactive / print
   262	   mode, the prompt argument, model selection, a machine-readable output format (JSON
   263	   if available), reasoning-effort controls, and read-only/sandbox/tool-allowlist.
   264	   Verify these against `--help` or the official docs and capture findings in
   265	   `research/` (include a small canary run if possible).
   266	2. Write the adapter in `src/adapters.ts` as an `xAdapter(model?, opts?)` factory that
   267	   returns a `Participant`. Reuse `runCli`, `spawnFailure`, and the `AgentResult`
   268	   shape. Parse the CLI output and classify success/failure on STRUCTURAL signals
   269	   (exit code + a success marker), not brittle text matches. Make `bin` overridable
   270	   to handle shadowed/stale shims.
   271	3. Wire it in (four sites): add the id to `AdapterId` and to the `ADAPTERS` /
   272	   `PARTICIPANT_KEYS` sets and error strings in `src/config.ts`; add a `case` to
   273	   `buildParticipant` in `src/index.ts`; if `bin` is overridable, include the id in
   274	   `BIN_OVERRIDABLE` in `src/install.ts`.
   275	4. Test it like the others: add a `test/fakes/<cli>` shim (copy `test/fakes/pi`) and a
   276	   captured fixture under `test/fixtures/`, then add classifier tests to
   277	   `test/adapters.test.ts` (success path, read-only flags, effort on/off, error path,
   278	   and `bin` override). Run `npm test`.
   279	5. Document it: update this README, `docs/3_ADAPTERS.md`, add a commented example to
   280	   `examples/debate.yaml`, and update CHANGELOG/version notes per project rules.
   281	6. Open an MR titled `vX.Y.Z <CLI> adapter` summarizing the headless recipe and the
   282	   read-only mechanism chosen.

   139	## How it works (v0)
   140	
   141	- **Cross-vendor** participants by design — default `claude` (Anthropic) + `codex`
   142	  (OpenAI); `agy` (Google/Gemini), `pi`, and `copilot-cli` via config — because
   143	  diversity of reasoning is the whole point.
   144	- Each agent turn runs in **isolation**: a throwaway temp dir, or — when you pass a
   145	  repo — a **detached throwaway git worktree of HEAD**, so agentic CLIs can't read
   146	  each other's outputs, and test runs / stray writes never touch your real checkout.
   147	- `claude` is read via its JSON envelope (success = `exit==0 && is_error==false`);
   148	  `codex` via its JSONL event stream (last `agent_message` + `turn.completed`);
   149	  `pi` ([earendil-works/pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi), a minimal,
   150	  low-token multi-LLM harness) via its `--mode json` event stream (last assistant
   151	  `message_end`); `copilot-cli` via GitHub Copilot CLI JSONL (`result.exitCode` +
   152	  last `assistant.message`); `agy` is text-only (stdout is the answer). All invocation
   153	  details are grounded in real local runs — see [`research/canary-results.md`](./research/canary-results.md)
   154	  and the per-CLI files in [`research/`](./research/).
   155	
   156	## The flow: phases & artifacts
   157	
   158	A run moves through these phases (scholastic names in parentheses — Disputatio models
   159	a medieval *disputatio*). Everything from the respondeo on is **opt-in**: it runs only
   160	when the config defines a `judge` (e.g. the opus judge `--init` seeds).
   161	
   162	1. **Proposals** (*videtur quod*, "it seems that…") — every agent independently answers
   163	   the quaestio, in isolation, so no one peeks at another's take. Needs ≥2 to succeed.
   164	2. **Reaction rounds** (*sed contra*, "but against this…") — each agent reacts
   165	   adversarially to the full transcript: where it agrees, where it disagrees (with
   166	   real flaws), what's missing — ideally backed by **executable evidence**. `--rounds N`.
   167	3. **Respondeo** (the judge's *consolidatio*, the determination) — one judge reads the
   168	   whole transcript and renders the verdict: the **settled agreements**, a **ruling on
   169	   each contested point** (favouring positions backed by run code over rhetoric), or —
   170	   when a point genuinely can't be settled from the transcript — a list of
   171	   **questions for you** (status `NEEDS_INPUT`) instead of a guessed answer.
   172	4. **Redactio** (the deliverable) — *only* when the respondeo resolves, the judge then
   173	   acts as **synthesizer** and writes the document you actually start the work from
   174	   (an implementation plan, a review, a proposal…), built from the settled decisions.
   175	   With `--repo` it grounds this in your real files (read-only).
   176	
   177	When the respondeo asks for input, you **close the loop** with
   178	`disputatio --continue "<your answers>"`: it folds your answers in and re-judges. If
   179	that resolves, the deliverable is drafted. (If your answer opens a question the
   180	debaters never argued, the judge says so rather than inventing a verdict — re-run the
   181	debate to bring them back in.)

   184	
   185	| File              | What it is                                                                    |
   186	| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   187	| `debate.md`       | the full transcript — proposals, reactions, and the respondeo                 |
   188	| `respondeo.md`    | the judge's ruling **on** the debate (versioned `-2`, `-3`… per `--continue`) |
   189	| `final-report.md` | the **redactio**: the deliverable born **from** the debate — start work here  |
   190	| `raw/`            | per-turn raw CLI captures, the only way to diagnose a failed turn             |
   191	
   192	> `respondeo.md` judges the debate; `final-report.md` is the product. They are
   193	> different documents on purpose — the verdict tells you *what was decided*, the
   194	> deliverable gives you *the thing to execute*.

   197

   216	### Supported adapters
   217	
   218	Currently supported adapters include:
   219	- `claude` -> https://code.claude.com/docs
   220	- `codex` -> https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli
   221	- `agy` -> https://antigravity.google/product/antigravity-cli
   222	- `pi` -> https://pi.dev
   223	- `copilot-cli` -> https://docs.github.com/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli

   226	implement the small transport layer that lets Disputatio treat different CLIs uniformly.
   227	
   228	### What an adapter is
   229	
   230	An adapter is Disputatio's anti-corruption boundary around one agent CLI. It does
   231	exactly one job: spawn the CLI in a sandboxed working directory, capture its output,
   232	and classify the run as success (`{ok:true, text}`) or failure (`{ok:false, error}`).
   233	Everything quirky about a given CLI — its flags, its output format (JSON envelope vs.
   234	JSONL stream vs. plain text), how it signals an error — is hidden here, so the debate
   235	logic never has to care which vendor it is talking to. The contract is the
   236	`Participant` type in [`src/adapters.ts`](./src/adapters.ts):
   237	
   238	```ts
   239	type Participant = {
   240	  id: string;       // short stable key ("claude", "codex", "pi", "copilot-cli")
   241	  display: string;  // human label, encodes model ("Pi (anthropic/claude...)")
   242	  vendor: string;   // used for the cross-vendor diversity check — keep it DISTINCT
   243	  run: (prompt: string, cwd: string) => Promise<AgentResult>;
   244	};
   245	```

   248	
   249	- **Read-only evidence.** The agent may inspect the repo but must never mutate it —
   250	  use the CLI's strongest read-only mechanism (OS sandbox if it has one, otherwise a
   251	  tool allowlist that omits write/edit/shell-exec). Disputatio already isolates each
   252	  turn in a throwaway temp dir / git worktree, but the adapter is the second defense.
   253	- **Cross-vendor diversity.** Give the adapter a `vendor` distinct from the others —
   254	  diversity of reasoning is the entire premise, and `index.ts` warns on a lineup that
   255	  isn't all-distinct vendors.

   265	   `research/` (include a small canary run if possible).

   268	   shape. Parse the CLI output and classify success/failure on STRUCTURAL signals

   270	   to handle shadowed/stale shims.

   273	   `buildParticipant` in `src/index.ts`; if `bin` is overridable, include the id in

    24	thing API-level multi-agent frameworks cannot easily reproduce, and it is what
    25	Disputatio is built around.

    32	## How to Run
    33	
    34	### Prerequisites
    35	
    36	- **Node ≥ 24**.
    37	- [`claude`](https://code.claude.com) and [`codex`](https://developers.openai.com/codex)
    38	  (default lineup) installed and **already authenticated** (authentication is out of
    39	  scope — log in to each CLI first). [`agy`](https://antigravity.google),
    40	  [`pi`](https://pi.dev), and [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://docs.github.com/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli)
    41	  are optional via `--config`. **Account hygiene matters:** only point a CLI at repositories its
    42	  credentials and policy are allowed to access.
    43	
    44	### Install and use
    45	
    46	Install the published CLI, then run `disputatio` from any repository:
    47	
    48	```bash
    49	npm install -g disputatio
    50	```
    51	
    52	After installing (and logging into each CLI), run **`disputatio --init`** once: it canaries
    53	the lineup, resolves each CLI's real binary (handling shadowed/stale installs), and writes a
    54	machine-tuned config to `~/.config/disputatio/config.yaml`. That file — not the shipped
    55	`examples/debate.yaml` (a copy-me **template**) — is what a no-`--config` run reads.
    56	
    57	**Config precedence (no `--config` given):** `~/.config/disputatio/config.yaml` if present,
    58	else the built-in lineup (`claude` + `codex`, no judge). An explicit `--config <path>` always wins.
    59	
    60	### Usage
    61	
    62	```bash
    63	# one-time setup after authenticating each CLI: detect binaries + write the user config
    64	# (with an opus judge seeded). --force overwrites an existing config (otherwise it's backed up).
    65	disputatio --init
    66	
    67	# preflight: canary every participant CLI (runnable + authenticated) before
    68	# spending tokens on a real debate. Exit 0 = all healthy, exit 1 = something's off.
    69	# Run this first, especially on a new machine.
    70	disputatio --doctor
    71	disputatio --doctor --config examples/debate.yaml   # check a specific lineup
    72	
    73	# one proposal round + one reaction round (pure reasoning, isolated temp dirs).
    74	# the quaestio is given inline — quote it so the shell passes it as one argument
    75	disputatio "Review changes in this branch and find issues."
    76	
    77	# for a long quaestio, read it from a markdown file instead
    78	disputatio --file examples/task.md
    79	
    80	# more reaction rounds
    81	disputatio "Review changes in this branch and find issues." --rounds 2
    82	
    83	# point the agents at a real repo so they can gather READ-ONLY evidence
    84	# (this is where the executable-evidence value actually lives);
    85	# agents work in a throwaway git worktree of HEAD, never your real checkout
    86	disputatio "Review changes in this branch and find issues." --repo /path/to/your/repo
    87	
    88	# choose the lineup/models/budgets/effort explicitly (see examples/debate.yaml).
    89	# per-participant `effort` doses token spend — claude: low|medium|high|xhigh|max;
    90	# codex: minimal|low|medium|high; agy: encode it in the model name (no effort key).
    91	disputatio --file path/to/task.md --rounds 1 --repo /path/to/your/repo --config examples/debate.yaml
    92	
    93	# --- closing the loop (when a judge ran) ---------------------------------------------
    94	
    95	# the judge ended in NEEDS_INPUT? answer its open questions and re-judge the latest
    96	# debate. If it now resolves, the final deliverable (final-report.md) is drafted too.
    97	disputatio --continue "Async translation; files are comment-free; translator hands files to a dev."
    98	
    99	# ground that deliverable in your real repo (read-only worktree of HEAD), and/or target
   100	# a specific past debate instead of the latest one:
   101	disputatio --continue "<answers>" --debate /path/to/repo/.debate/debate-<ts> --repo /path/to/repo
   102	
   103	# (re)draft final-report.md from an already-resolved debate (no re-judging)
   104	disputatio --finalize --debate .debate/debate-<ts> [--repo /path/to/your/repo]
   105	```
   106	
   107	Output lands in `.debate/debate-<timestamp>/` (see [the flow](#the-flow-phases--artifacts)
   108	below for what each file is). The **path printed to stdout** is the primary artifact —
   109	the deliverable (`final-report.md`) when one was produced, otherwise the transcript
   110	(`debate.md`); all progress goes to stderr. If fewer than two proposals succeed the
   111	debate **aborts with exit 1** (a one-voice "debate" is worthless) — the partial
   112	transcript and raw captures are kept.

   116	If you are working from a clone of this repository, Node 24 can execute the TypeScript
   117	entry point directly, so there is no build step for local development. Use the same
   118	commands as above, replacing `disputatio` with `node src/index.ts`:

   122	node src/index.ts "Review changes in this branch and find issues."

   139	## How it works (v0)
   140	
   141	- **Cross-vendor** participants by design — default `claude` (Anthropic) + `codex`
   142	  (OpenAI); `agy` (Google/Gemini), `pi`, and `copilot-cli` via config — because
   143	  diversity of reasoning is the whole point.
   144	- Each agent turn runs in **isolation**: a throwaway temp dir, or — when you pass a
   145	  repo — a **detached throwaway git worktree of HEAD**, so agentic CLIs can't read
   146	  each other's outputs, and test runs / stray writes never touch your real checkout.
   147	- `claude` is read via its JSON envelope (success = `exit==0 && is_error==false`);
   148	  `codex` via its JSONL event stream (last `agent_message` + `turn.completed`);
   149	  `pi` ([earendil-works/pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi), a minimal,
   150	  low-token multi-LLM harness) via its `--mode json` event stream (last assistant
   151	  `message_end`); `copilot-cli` via GitHub Copilot CLI JSONL (`result.exitCode` +
   152	  last `assistant.message`); `agy` is text-only (stdout is the answer). All invocation
   153	  details are grounded in real local runs — see [`research/canary-results.md`](./research/canary-results.md)
   154	  and the per-CLI files in [`research/`](./research/).
   155	
   156	## The flow: phases & artifacts
   157	
   158	A run moves through these phases (scholastic names in parentheses — Disputatio models
   159	a medieval *disputatio*). Everything from the respondeo on is **opt-in**: it runs only
   160	when the config defines a `judge` (e.g. the opus judge `--init` seeds).
   161	
   162	1. **Proposals** (*videtur quod*, "it seems that…") — every agent independently answers
   163	   the quaestio, in isolation, so no one peeks at another's take. Needs ≥2 to succeed.
   164	2. **Reaction rounds** (*sed contra*, "but against this…") — each agent reacts
   165	   adversarially to the full transcript: where it agrees, where it disagrees (with
   166	   real flaws), what's missing — ideally backed by **executable evidence**. `--rounds N`.
   167	3. **Respondeo** (the judge's *consolidatio*, the determination) — one judge reads the
   168	   whole transcript and renders the verdict: the **settled agreements**, a **ruling on
   169	   each contested point** (favouring positions backed by run code over rhetoric), or —
   170	   when a point genuinely can't be settled from the transcript — a list of
   171	   **questions for you** (status `NEEDS_INPUT`) instead of a guessed answer.
   172	4. **Redactio** (the deliverable) — *only* when the respondeo resolves, the judge then
   173	   acts as **synthesizer** and writes the document you actually start the work from
   174	   (an implementation plan, a review, a proposal…), built from the settled decisions.
   175	   With `--repo` it grounds this in your real files (read-only).
   176	
   177	When the respondeo asks for input, you **close the loop** with
   178	`disputatio --continue "<your answers>"`: it folds your answers in and re-judges. If
   179	that resolves, the deliverable is drafted. (If your answer opens a question the
   180	debaters never argued, the judge says so rather than inventing a verdict — re-run the
   181	debate to bring them back in.)
   182	
   183	**What you get in `.debate/debate-<timestamp>/`:**
   184	
   185	| File              | What it is                                                                    |
   186	| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   187	| `debate.md`       | the full transcript — proposals, reactions, and the respondeo                 |
   188	| `respondeo.md`    | the judge's ruling **on** the debate (versioned `-2`, `-3`… per `--continue`) |
   189	| `final-report.md` | the **redactio**: the deliverable born **from** the debate — start work here  |
   190	| `raw/`            | per-turn raw CLI captures, the only way to diagnose a failed turn             |
   191	
   192	> `respondeo.md` judges the debate; `final-report.md` is the product. They are
   193	> different documents on purpose — the verdict tells you *what was decided*, the
   194	> deliverable gives you *the thing to execute*.
   195	
   196	## Known v0 limitations (next steps)
   197	
   198	- No scholastic **`consolidatio` as a pre-debate step** (merging N proposals into one
   199	  shared object for the skeptics to attack), no structured contribution trailer /
   200	  evidence-typing yet. The `respondeo` (verdict) and `redactio` (deliverable) phases
   201	  **do** exist.
   202	- `--continue` re-judges **alone**; it does not yet re-engage the debaters when your
   203	  answer opens genuinely new ground (it flags that case instead). A crashed run is not
   204	  resumable — it accumulates in memory and writes at the end, so restart from scratch.
   205	- Reaction rounds are parallel snapshots (agents react to proposals, not to each
   206	  other's same-round reactions).
   207	- Timeout kills the whole **process group** (`SIGTERM`, then `SIGKILL` after a short
   208	  grace), so a slow turn can't wedge the run by leaking a worker that holds the output
   209	  pipe open (lesson from the 2026-06-12 repo-grounded run).
   210	- Evidence mode shows agents **HEAD only** (uncommitted changes are invisible) and
   211	  untracked build artifacts (`node_modules`, …) are absent from the worktree, so
   212	  some test suites won't run there.

   214	## Adapters
   215	
   216	### Supported adapters
   217	
   218	Currently supported adapters include:
   219	- `claude` -> https://code.claude.com/docs
   220	- `codex` -> https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli
   221	- `agy` -> https://antigravity.google/product/antigravity-cli
   222	- `pi` -> https://pi.dev
   223	- `copilot-cli` -> https://docs.github.com/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli
   224	
   225	Each adapter lives in `src/adapters.ts` and has per-CLI notes in `docs/3_ADAPTERS.md`. The adapters
   226	implement the small transport layer that lets Disputatio treat different CLIs uniformly.
   227	
   228	### What an adapter is
   229	
   230	An adapter is Disputatio's anti-corruption boundary around one agent CLI. It does
   231	exactly one job: spawn the CLI in a sandboxed working directory, capture its output,
   232	and classify the run as success (`{ok:true, text}`) or failure (`{ok:false, error}`).
   233	Everything quirky about a given CLI — its flags, its output format (JSON envelope vs.
   234	JSONL stream vs. plain text), how it signals an error — is hidden here, so the debate
   235	logic never has to care which vendor it is talking to. The contract is the
   236	`Participant` type in [`src/adapters.ts`](./src/adapters.ts):
   237	
   238	```ts
   239	type Participant = {
   240	  id: string;       // short stable key ("claude", "codex", "pi", "copilot-cli")
   241	  display: string;  // human label, encodes model ("Pi (anthropic/claude...)")
   242	  vendor: string;   // used for the cross-vendor diversity check — keep it DISTINCT
   243	  run: (prompt: string, cwd: string) => Promise<AgentResult>;
   244	};
   245	```
   246	
   247	Two invariants every adapter must honor (both are correctness, not style):
   248	
   249	- **Read-only evidence.** The agent may inspect the repo but must never mutate it —
   250	  use the CLI's strongest read-only mechanism (OS sandbox if it has one, otherwise a
   251	  tool allowlist that omits write/edit/shell-exec). Disputatio already isolates each
   252	  turn in a throwaway temp dir / git worktree, but the adapter is the second defense.
   253	- **Cross-vendor diversity.** Give the adapter a `vendor` distinct from the others —
   254	  diversity of reasoning is the entire premise, and `index.ts` warns on a lineup that
   255	  isn't all-distinct vendors.
   256	
   257	### How to add a new adapter
   258	
   259	Recipe / checklist for adding a new adapter (follow TDD and keep the repo runnable):
   260	
   261	1. Research the CLI's headless mode first. Find the flags for non-interactive / print
   262	   mode, the prompt argument, model selection, a machine-readable output format (JSON
   263	   if available), reasoning-effort controls, and read-only/sandbox/tool-allowlist.
   264	   Verify these against `--help` or the official docs and capture findings in
   265	   `research/` (include a small canary run if possible).
   266	2. Write the adapter in `src/adapters.ts` as an `xAdapter(model?, opts?)` factory that
   267	   returns a `Participant`. Reuse `runCli`, `spawnFailure`, and the `AgentResult`
   268	   shape. Parse the CLI output and classify success/failure on STRUCTURAL signals
   269	   (exit code + a success marker), not brittle text matches. Make `bin` overridable
   270	   to handle shadowed/stale shims.
   271	3. Wire it in (four sites): add the id to `AdapterId` and to the `ADAPTERS` /
   272	   `PARTICIPANT_KEYS` sets and error strings in `src/config.ts`; add a `case` to
   273	   `buildParticipant` in `src/index.ts`; if `bin` is overridable, include the id in
   274	   `BIN_OVERRIDABLE` in `src/install.ts`.
   275	4. Test it like the others: add a `test/fakes/<cli>` shim (copy `test/fakes/pi`) and a
   276	   captured fixture under `test/fixtures/`, then add classifier tests to
   277	   `test/adapters.test.ts` (success path, read-only flags, effort on/off, error path,
   278	   and `bin` override). Run `npm test`.
   279	5. Document it: update this README, `docs/3_ADAPTERS.md`, add a commented example to
   280	   `examples/debate.yaml`, and update CHANGELOG/version notes per project rules.
   281	6. Open an MR titled `vX.Y.Z <CLI> adapter` summarizing the headless recipe and the
   282	   read-only mechanism chosen.
